title.zh-TW: Antigravity 也有額度狀態列，開關會自己補齊
title.en: Antigravity gets the quota status line, and its switch keeps it current

body.zh-TW: 你若同時用 Claude Code 和 Antigravity CLI，面板的狀態列（status line，顯示在終端機最底下）開關，現在也會把額度顯示裝到後者；未裝 Antigravity 不建資料夾或檔案。macOS 把掛鉤（hook，事件觸發的小程式）放進 `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/`，由內建 `/usr/bin/python3` 執行，因此不依賴 App 的虛擬環境。像在兩台車上加同款儀表板：原來那台會先備份，關掉開關時再還原。新腳本會留著，免得正在啟動的 CLI 撞上刪檔，整個工作階段都出錯。已開啟者會在啟動時補裝遺失檔案、更新不同版本腳本；關掉就不會再裝。用 `pip` 或 `uv` 安裝也會帶上此掛鉤，Windows 系統匣等非 macOS 平台不碰 Antigravity 設定，避免寫入 `/usr/bin/python3`。
body.en: If you use both Claude Code and the Antigravity CLI, the panel's existing status line (the readout at the bottom of a terminal) switch now puts the same quota display on Antigravity too. Machines without Antigravity remain untouched: no folder or file is created. On macOS it places a hook (a small program triggered by an event) in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/` and runs it with built-in `/usr/bin/python3`, independent of the app's virtual environment. Think of fitting matching dashboards to two cars: your existing dashboard is backed up first and restored when you turn the switch off. The new script stays behind so a CLI already starting does not collide with its deletion and show an error for its whole session. Startup replaces a missing or outdated script only while the switch is on. `pip` and `uv` installs now include it; non-macOS platforms leave Antigravity settings alone, avoiding `/usr/bin/python3` on Windows.

items.original:
**The status line switch now covers the Antigravity CLI too.** The panel's single switch has always installed Claude Code's status line; it now mirrors the same quota display onto Antigravity when its CLI is installed. The hook is copied to `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/` and runs under macOS's built-in `/usr/bin/python3`, so it stays stdlib-only and independent of the app's virtual environment. A status line you configured yourself is backed up to a sidecar file first and restored when the switch is turned off; the deployed script is deliberately left behind, because deleting it races with any CLI that is starting and would leave that session showing a status line error for its whole lifetime. A machine without the Antigravity CLI is untouched — no directory and no file is created, and the switch keeps working for Claude Code exactly as before.
**Startup self-healing keeps the Antigravity status line current.** Installing it only on the switch's rising edge would have hidden the feature from everyone whose switch was already on, and would have frozen the deployed script at whatever version first installed it. Self-heal now reinstalls it when it is missing and re-copies it when its bytes differ from the bundled source, both gated on the switch being on — so turning the switch off keeps it off. The Antigravity branch is isolated from the rest of self-heal and only records a log entry when the install actually succeeds.
**`pip` and `uv` installs ship the Antigravity hook.** `usage_statusline_agy` was missing from `py-modules`, so a non-bundle install could not resolve the script and the switch silently did nothing for Antigravity.
**Non-macOS platforms no longer touch Antigravity's settings.** The Windows tray shares the same toggle, and `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` expands there too, so a Windows user with the CLI would have had `/usr/bin/python3` written into their configuration. The sync is now a no-op off macOS.

title.zh-TW: 短暫高用量不再被判成 Heavy
title.en: A brief burst no longer marks you Heavy

body.zh-TW: 剛送出一則內容很多的訊息，狀態卻立刻把你標成 Heavy，現在不會這麼快下結論。先前 burn rate（用量燃燒率，把 token 除以經過時間算出的速度）最短拿一分鐘來算；單則訊息的快取（cache，把算過或查過的結果暫存起來直接用）建立 token（AI 處理與計費的文字單位）就可能把數字推得很高。現在最短觀察時間改成五分鐘，跟 `burn_rate.py` 原本用來預估的下限一致。這像用車速表判斷你是否超速：不能只看起步那一下的猛踩，得看一小段路。它不是把用量藏起來，而是少讓短暫尖峰替你貼上重度使用者標籤。
body.en: After you send one especially large message, the status display will no longer rush to label you Heavy. Burn rate (the pace calculated by dividing tokens, units of AI text processing and billing, by elapsed time) used to use a span as short as one minute. Cache creation from one message could therefore push the rate high on its own. The shortest span is now five minutes, matching the forecasting floor already used by `burn_rate.py`. It is like judging speed from a car's gauge: you cannot call someone a speeder from one hard press at the starting line; you need a short stretch of road. Usage is not hidden; a brief spike is simply less likely to attach a heavy-user label.

items.original: **A short burst no longer classifies you as a heavy user.** Burn-rate classification divided tokens by an elapsed span as small as one minute, so a single message's cache-creation tokens could produce a rate high enough for Heavy on their own. The minimum span is now five minutes, matching the forecast floor `burn_rate.py` already used.

title.zh-TW: 兩個選單開關並排，少一條多餘分隔線
title.en: Two menu toggles now sit together without a misleading divider

body.zh-TW: 打開選單想調整兩個開關時，現在它們會排在同一組，中間那條分隔線拿掉了。兩者原本都是單純的開／關選項，線條卻像在菜單上把同類配菜切成兩區，讓人以為它們有不同身分或用途。畫面沒有增加新控制項，也沒有改掉任何一個開關能做的事；只是讓排列跟實際關係一致。你看到兩個並列開關，就知道它們同樣是可獨立啟用或停用的選項，不必猜那條線暗示了什麼差別。
body.en: When you open the menu to adjust its two toggles, they now appear as one group, with the separator between them removed. Both were always simple on/off controls, but the line was like splitting matching side dishes into separate sections of a menu: it suggested they had different roles. No new control has appeared, and neither toggle does anything different. The layout now matches their actual relationship. Seeing two switches side by side tells you they are both options you can turn on or off independently, without making you guess what distinction the divider was meant to signal.

items.original: The menu's two toggles are grouped together without the separator that used to sit between them; both are plain on/off switches, so the divider implied a distinction that does not exist.
